The menu-bar window opened on the other display, not under the icon
error: The menu-bar window opened on the other display, not under the icon
fix: Find the monitor containing the icon, use that monitor's scale, clamp to its edges, and set the position again after show (macOS converts the first move with the old screen's scale).
root_cause: The icon's rectangle was converted to physical pixels with the tray window's own scale factor, which is the scale of the screen it was last on; with two displays of different scale the position landed on the wrong screen.

detail: Choose… (a folder dialog) took about 20 seconds to open
error: Choose… (a folder dialog) took about 20 seconds to open
fix: src-tauri/src/folder_panel.rs keeps one NSOpenPanel for the app's life and reuses it; every folder button calls choose_folders instead of the dialog plugin's open().
root_cause: On macOS 27 a second NSOpenPanel in one process waits ~26 s in -[NSSavePanel _initBridgeAndStuff] on its out-of-process view service (measured in a bare Swift app: 0.5 s first, 26 s second; reusing the first panel is instant). tauri-plugin-dialog makes a new panel every time.

detail: Folder dialogs still waited 20-26 s, the first one of a run too, in Keepr and other non-sandboxed apps
error: Folder dialogs still waited 20-26 s, the first one of a run too, in Keepr and other non-sandboxed apps
fix: Nothing to change in Keepr beyond the reused panel; the stuck cloud provider has to be restarted or re-signed-in. Diagnose with: sample the openAndSavePanelService pid during the wait, and fileproviderctl dump.
root_cause: Not Keepr: the open-panel helper blocks in TNode::RootFPItemsForDomainsWithTimeout waiting for every File Provider domain's root item for the sidebar; a cloud domain whose extension isn't running (fileproviderctl dump shows it 'without connection' for the openAndSavePanelService servicers) makes every new panel wait out the timeout. Reusing one panel (folder_panel.rs) avoids the wait after the first.

detail: Slow folder dialogs on the dev Mac were fixed outside Keepr: restarting a disconnected cloud File Provider, then turning iCloud Drive on and off again (it was off while signed in to iCloud, and the panel waited on its root item). After that every new NSOpenPanel took under 0.6 s. Keepr keeps reusing one panel regardless.
The SMB dialogs didn't list a server's shares, and found no servers
error: The SMB dialogs didn't list a server's shares, and found no servers
fix: Shares show as buttons; -N goes before the server; Bonjour is browsed with DNSServiceBrowse directly; servers Keepr uses or has mounted are offered too (a network may have no SMB servers on Bonjour at all).
root_cause: Three things: shares went into an HTML datalist, which shows nothing until you type; for a guest login -N came after the server, where smbutil stops reading options; and dns-sd -B buffers its output when not writing to a terminal, so reading it for a second got nothing.

detail: Keepr can't write there: Operation not supported (os error 45) on an SMB share
error: Keepr can't write there: Operation not supported (os error 45) on an SMB share
fix: keepr_engine::backend::sync falls back to fsync(2) on ENOTSUP/EINVAL/ENOTTY; used by the backend, restore and the destination test. Confirmed on a real share: F_FULLFSYNC -> 45, fsync ok.
root_cause: On macOS, Rust's File::sync_all issues fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC), which smbfs refuses with ENOTSUP; the destination test, every pack and index write, and restores all called it.

root_cause: Every overview refresh (30 s timer and each 'changed' event) reset the list to its first page, and a scroll load that hit the in-flight flag was dropped with nothing to retrigger it

Restore tree repeats a folder's files each time it is collapsed and expanded
error: Restore tree repeats a folder's files each time it is collapsed and expanded
fix: Rows keyed by their place in the tree; save_plan refuses a source that is inside another (config::overlapping_sources)
root_cause: The plan backed up a folder and a folder inside it as two sources, so the snapshot held the same path twice; Restore keyed rows by path, and the duplicate React keys left rows behind on collapse

detail: Restore tree still repeats files after keying rows by joined names
error: Restore tree still repeats files after keying rows by joined names
fix: Rows keyed by sibling position (parent key + '.' + index); verified in headless Chrome against a mocked backend with nested sources
root_cause: A source's entry name is its whole path, so parent key + '/' + name for a folder inside the Keepr source equalled the key of the nested source's own root row

error: One failed Keychain read (Deny, locked, no one to answer) then saving any secret erased every plan password and recovery key

root_cause: keychain::load treated every failed read or unparsable item as an empty map and cached it, so the next set() wrote that near-empty map over the whole item

error: Listing SMB shares could leak pty file descriptors or leave smbutil waiting at its prompt

error: S3 source sheet says 'Its key is in your Keychain' and enables Add with no secret after switching service or access key

detail: Repo::open fails: damaged data (index file over 64 MiB once decompressed)
error: Repo::open fails: damaged data (index file over 64 MiB once decompressed)
fix: Index files and snapshots decompress as a stream; write_index starts a new file every INDEX_ENTRIES blobs
root_cause: decode capped zstd output at 64 MiB when no plain length was known, and flush/prune wrote one unbounded index file; ~670k blobs passed the cap

detail: Snapshot saved pointing at chunks that are not in any pack after a pack write failed
error: Snapshot saved pointing at chunks that are not in any pack after a pack write failed
fix: write_pack records the failure; flush indexes what was written, then fails, so backup::run saves no snapshot
root_cause: write_pack failing only failed the thread that filled the pack; other threads had been told their blobs were stored, and flush succeeded

detail: Prune deletes packs written by a --back-up run as leftovers
error: Prune deletes packs written by a --back-up run as leftovers
fix: prune run, remove_path and remove_source reload the index right after taking the exclusive lock; load_index keeps this session's unindexed packs
root_cause: reclaim used the in-memory index of a Repo kept open by the app, which lacked packs another process indexed since

detail: Restore from a bucket backup can write outside the chosen folder
error: Restore from a bucket backup can write outside the chosen folder

detail: An unreadable folder is backed up empty and stays empty in later FSEvents backups
error: An unreadable folder is backed up empty and stays empty in later FSEvents backups
fix: On a listing or metadata error, keep the previous snapshot's node (as for unreadable files) and note the error
root_cause: Walk::dir saved an empty folder on read_dir failure and silently dropped entries whose listing or metadata failed

detail: keep_deleted_days misses a recently deleted file in a big snapshot
error: keep_deleted_days misses a recently deleted file in a big snapshot

detail: Plan stuck retrying every 5 minutes with a failure notification each time
error: Plan stuck retrying every 5 minutes with a failure notification each time
fix: Core::run clears waiting whenever a backup ends with any result other than waiting
root_cause: PlanState.waiting was cleared only on success or a manual Back Up; a later failure for another reason left it set, so the scheduler kept the 5-minute waiting retry

detail: A running Keepr's lock on this Mac is cleared as stale after 24 hours
error: A running Keepr's lock on this Mac is cleared as stale after 24 hours
fix: Same host: stale only when its pid is gone; a thread refreshes the lock time hourly; re-check after writing and back off on conflict
root_cause: Lock staleness applied the 24h age rule to same-host locks with a live pid; locks were never refreshed; check-then-write raced

detail: App freezes (beachball) when an SMB destination's mount has gone dead, or on a Keychain prompt
error: App freezes (beachball) when an SMB destination's mount has gone dead, or on a Keychain prompt

root_cause: Every changed event rebuilt the tray icon via overview_of on the main thread (statfs/canonicalize per destination, history clone); overview and the Keychain commands were sync commands, also on the main thread

detail: S3 read fails at once when the connection drops during the body
error: S3 read fails at once when the connection drops during the body
fix: read/read_at go through S3::get, which retries the whole request and body read
root_cause: send retried only until headers arrived; body read errors and short bodies were not retried

detail: Duplicate jobs queued; CLI --back-up/--remove-path could exit mid-backup
error: Duplicate jobs queued; CLI --back-up/--remove-path could exit mid-backup
fix: Job is popped and installed as current under the queue lock; queue lock is always taken before current's; Core::idle checks both under it
root_cause: The job thread popped a job and only later set current in run(); in the gap it was neither queued nor running

detail: A chunk is stored twice when seen again during a pack upload
error: A chunk is stored twice when seen again during a pack upload
fix: Packer keeps an inflight set, checked by add, until the index has the pack's blobs
root_cause: take() emptied pending before the pack reached the index, so during the upload a blob was in neither

detail: config.json/state.json lost: empty after a power cut, or replaced by defaults after a read error
error: config.json/state.json lost: empty after a power cut, or replaced by defaults after a read error

detail: Prune pack size error hidden, then size - live_bytes underflows
